title: Chapter architecture
recall_points: Status and historical perspective → reasons for inequality → safeguards → women’s organisations → role models and way forward

title: Life cycle of discrimination
recall_points: Early age: neglected care and education, sexual abuse, physical violence
Adolescence: early marriage/pregnancy, sexual and domestic violence, dowry harassment, marital rape, son preference, desertion, maternal mortality
Older women/widows: witch-hunt, desertion, emotional/social/financial neglect, feminisation of elderly
Sex selection before birth → deprivation and violence in childhood → marriage/reproductive coercion → neglect and widowhood in old age

title: Global Gender Gap Index
recall_points: Economic participation/opportunity: LFPR, wage equality, estimated earned income
Educational attainment: literacy and primary/secondary/tertiary enrolment
Health and survival: sex ratio at birth, healthy life expectancy
Political empowerment: parliamentary/ministerial representation, years with female/male head of state
Economic opportunity, education, health and political power are distinct dimensions → one aggregate score can conceal uneven parity
Education and health scores are close to parity
Economic participation and political empowerment scores are much lower

title: Women’s employment and unpaid work
recall_points: Unpaid domestic/care work consumes time → fewer paid-work opportunities → lower female labour-force participation

title: Representation and gender norms
recall_points: Disapproval of married women working when husbands earn well → social restriction independent of financial need → lower participation

title: Women’s health, early marriage and education
recall_points: Women are about half of higher-education/PhD enrolment
Their undergraduate engineering share is much lower

title: Vedic and medieval status
recall_points: Pastoral/nomadic economy → no economic surplus/private property → egalitarianism
Agriculture → division of labour → Grihapathi control over women
Gargi and Maitreyi → Sabhas and Samitis
Stridharma, Pativratadharma, ritual purification and fasts
Polygamy, purdah and talaq: continued prejudices

title: Colonial social reform
recall_points: British education → emergence of a new elite → questioning existing social practices

Pandita Ramabai → Sharda Sadan for destitute widows

Parvati Bhore and Ushabai Dange → communist textile-worker leaders
Political participation and collective struggle → recognition of women’s claims → constitutional voting rights and equality

title: Telangana movement and post-independence legislation
recall_points: Oppression by Nizam, Patils and Jagirdars
Exploitative Deshmukhs, Despandes and tax collectors
Vetti forced labour → exploitation of peasant girls

title: Chipko and women’s livelihoods
recall_points: Food, fodder, fuel, fibre, fertilizer → forest-linked livelihood needs → self-sufficiency
Adwani, Tehri Garhwal district of UP
Hugging trees and tying sacred thread
Gaura Devi stopped contractors/forest personnel entering Reni forest
Women defended forest-linked food, fodder, fuel, fibre and fertilizer → protection of livelihoods and self-sufficiency through collective action

title: Anti-rape and anti-dowry movements
recall_points: Elite: cultural activities and beauty pageants
Poor/rural: peasant conditions, wife beating, alcoholism, dowry, sexual harassment
Mathura rape incident → protests and petitions → powerful people cannot violate poor/powerless people’s dignity and rights
Campaign against dowry, abetment to suicide and murder
Dowry demand recognised as potentially abetting suicide

title: Waves of feminism
recall_points: First: education, widows’ rights, child marriage; Ramabai, Savitribai Phule, Rukhmabai
Second: gender inequality, reproductive rights, violence, dowry; AIWC/university women’s studies centres
Third: intersectionality, gender justice, Dalit/marginalised rights
Gender justice connected with Dalit and marginalised rights → attention to overlapping forms of disadvantage

title: Structural reasons for women’s inequality
recall_points: Caste boundary maintenance → control of property and sexuality → disinheritance, arranged marriage, child marriage
Purity associated with Anuloma and Pratiloma
Husband and his parents make life choices
Pregnancy and child rearing → employment loss
Patriarchal, patrilocal, patrilineal family reinforces control
Son preference in funeral pyre and Shradha rituals
Discriminatory religious personal laws; example: triple talaq
Poor implementation of laws + patriarchal family/religious norms + economic restrictions + normalised misogyny → formal protection fails to transform lived status
Higher-caste restrictions overlap with class position
Upper-caste women engaged in unpaid domestic work
Control of women maintains caste boundaries

title: Meaning and pillars of empowerment
recall_points: Making life choices and reaching full potential
Health → nutrition, delayed marriage, reproductive authority
Economic → safe work, skills, SHGs, equal pay
Political → local-body reservation and parliamentary representation
Empowerment requires women’s control over reproductive decisions → health and autonomy beyond simply managing fertility

title: From welfare to agency
recall_points: Development → health, education, employment; worker organisation/unionisation
Empowerment → SHGs, gender budgeting, enabling environment, local reservation
Later focus → gender equity and women’s agency
Committee on Status of Women in India (CSWI) → Towards Equality
STEP → Support to Training and Employment
AGP → Awareness Generation Programme for rural and poor women
Working girls’ hostels and Short Stay Homes
Twelfth Plan onwards: gender equity, women’s agency and empowerment
Committee on Status of Women in India

title: Constitutional safeguards
recall_points: Affirmative action → targeted support for women
Both advance substantive access and opportunity

title: BNS, family courts and interfaith marriage

recall_points: Beyond threshold, substantial foetal abnormality → state/institution Medical Board

recall_points: Children observe violence → learn to regard it as normal → normalisation of violent behaviour
Subjective interpretation of verbal abuse and mental harassment

recall_points: Violation of women’s dignity/right to life

recall_points: Gender lens applied to public spending

recall_points: Summoning, requisitioning records, evidence and affidavits

title: PMMVY and maternal-support comparison
recall_points: Partly compensate wage loss around childbirth
JSY/Janani Suraksha Yojana → encourage institutional delivery; cash incentive
PMMVY/Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana → rest/maternal care; maternity cash benefit
JSSK/Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakaram → remove costs at public facilities; free healthcare/transport
Pregnant women using public facilities and sick infants
Free delivery, medicines, tests, diet and transport
JSY: state-category rules; eligible-facility delivery; NHM; amount varies by state/rural–urban location
PMMVY: eligible pregnant/lactating women; care/registration/immunisation conditions; Mission Shakti–Samarthya
JSSK: public-facility users/sick infants; NHM; free services
PMMVY partly offsets wage loss/rest costs
Different barriers addressed by different benefits
